chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yunus, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the minimum act that, if a man performs it with a woman who is not permissible for his son or his father, he said: 'The limit in that is intimate contact, whether outward or inward, that resembles the touching of the two private parts.'

key_terms.بَاطِنَةً: Inwardly/externally (in terms of depth or nature)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum act of intimacy that establishes a legal boundary for a woman not permissible for a man's son or father?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the precise threshold of sexual intimacy that triggers specific legal consequences, such as the prohibition of marriage (mahram relationships) or the application of hadd punishments. The Imam defines the minimum act as 'mubaharah'—any contact resembling the touching of the private parts, whether external or internal—demonstrating the juristic focus on physical proximity and sensation rather than full penetration for this specific ruling.
